title: F7: tournament-style raw-JSON I/O doesn't survive a port without an adapter
description:
Symptom: every benchmark port (FFT, LLL, Stoer-Wagner, …) will need to translate between raw JSON (numbers, strings, arrays) and sci-wb canonical kinds. The 02-NTT port needed a hand-written adapter (scripts/validate-tournament-ntt.ts).

Fix: ship a packages/json-bridge with two operations:
  - jsonToCanonical(json: unknown, hint: KindHint): Value
  - canonicalToJson(value: Value): unknown
where KindHint annotates which raw fields should become integer vs float64 vs string (since '1.5' could be either). Optionally expose this as tools/json-canonicalize / tools/json-decanonicalize so adapters compose at the pipeline level.

Acceptance: rewrite scripts/validate-tournament-ntt.ts to use the bridge; line count should drop ~50%.
notes: Resolved 2026-04-28. Shipped @workbench/json-bridge package with hint-driven jsonToCanonical (raw JSON + Value-shaped hint tree → canonical Value) and canonicalToJson (canonical → raw, with integerEncoding/rationalEncoding/float64Encoding dials). 32 unit tests covering every kind, both directions, round-trip, error paths. Mutation-proven the tests catch regression. Refactored scripts/validate-tournament-ntt.ts to use the bridge (~30 lines of hand-rolled translation collapse to a hint declaration + 2 calls); 64/64 tournament cases still pass. Doc surfaces: packages/json-bridge/README.md (literate, comprehensive), package source itself is literate-style.

title: F1+F2: spawn machinery silently fails when BUN_BIN points to a snap symlink
description:
Symptoms: every script that spawns a tool subprocess (generate-goldens, check, oracle, registry-list, registry-search, the validator) either errors with cryptic 'cannot join mount namespace' / ENOENT, or returns silently empty results when the bun binary path isn't resolvable.

Root cause: process.env BUN_BIN defaults to the literal string 'bun', which resolves via PATH to /snap/bin/bun (a symlink) on snap installs. spawn() through that symlink fails namespace isolation. Even with BUN_BIN set, registry-search and other consumers swallow describeTool failures with bare `catch { continue; }` so the error surface is just an empty list.

Fix:
  1. packages/contract: in registry.ts, do realpathSync on BUN_BIN/PATH-resolved bun before first spawn; cache the resolved path.
  2. registry-search and similar: replace silent catches with stderr logging + a result counter so empty-due-to-failure is distinguishable from empty-by-filter.
  3. scripts/generate-goldens, scripts/check, tools/oracle, scripts/validate-tournament-ntt: use the same resolver from contract.
  4. README §Substrate: add a one-liner about snap installs.
notes: Resolved 2026-04-28. packages/contract/src/spawn.ts owns bun resolution; uses process.execPath when running under bun (the snap-confined corner) + PATH fallback + realpath collapse + smoke-test. Migrated all 5 internal call sites (registry.ts, oracle, generate-goldens, check, validate-tournament-ntt). registry-search now logs describe failures to stderr with a tally line. Verified: full check passes with BUN_BIN unset; bad BUN_BIN gives loud error. Doc surfaces updated: docs/adr/0001-subprocess-plumbing.md, packages/contract/README.md, README.md §Substrate, CLAUDE.md.

title: Friction-elimination iteration on scientist-workbench
description: After porting tstournament 02-NTT into sci-wb, 9 distinct frictions surfaced across the spawn machinery, scaffolder, protocol shape, conventions, and docs. This epic tracks driving each one to zero so the workbench is frictionless for the next port.
notes:
Three load-bearing collaboration principles surfaced mid-iteration (2026-04-28):
1. Rigorously keep docs up to date — every code change ships with paired doc updates.
2. Literate programming — code is exposition, prose-dominant, intent and impl interleaved.
3. Ground truth first before coding — establish spec/ADR/fixtures, verify current file state, then implement.

These supersede 'efficient implementation' as the dominant style. Each F-issue must include a docs-pass step (per-tool README, main README, PRD, CLAUDE.md, ADR if applicable) — done in the same cycle as the code.
Closed 2026-04-28. All 9 child issues resolved (8 friction items + 1 doubled root cause). Substrate now: subprocess plumbing centralised (ADR-0001), scaffolder accepts --uses (F3), schema kind annotations via kindOf (ADR-0002), error-pattern decision (ADR-0003) with mod-inv migrated, json-bridge package shipped (F7), raw-kind-literal lint phase added to scripts/check.ts (F6), example-count and TDD discipline doc-pinned (F4, F9). Three core principles codified in CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude memory: docs in lockstep, literate programming, ground truth before code. Full check (now 14 phases) green. Tournament cross-validation: 64/64.

title: tools/integrate-1d: adaptive Gauss-Kronrod 1D quadrature (G7K15)
description:
## Background

Second tool in the numerical tier (after linalg-solve, ADR-0014). The
orchestrator has prepared:

- `tools/integrate-1d/reference/manifest.json` — 30 cases generated by
  `scipy.integrate.quad` (QUADPACK QAGS) cross-validated against
  mpmath at 50-digit precision. The orthogonal oracle.
- A brief naming the algorithm (adaptive G7K15 with global priority-
  queue bisection) and the contract (numerical: true per ADR-0015,
  three boundary categories per ADR-0003).

## Fix

Build:

- `packages/quadrature/` — pure-TS library with
  `gaussKronrodAdaptive(f, a, b, opts)` and a tiny `evalNumericExpr`
  over the closed vocabulary `+ - * / ^ neg exp sin cos tan log sqrt
  abs` and constants `pi`, `e`. G7K15 nodes/weights from QUADPACK
  `dqk15.f` / GSL `qk15.c`. Algebraic-exactness tests on `x^k` for
  k=0..15. Mutation-prove the priority queue and Kronrod estimate.
- `tools/integrate-1d/` — wire-encoding wrapper. Schema:
  `record { f: any, var: symbol, a: float64, b: float64 }` →
  `record { value, error_estimate, n_evals, converged, iterations,
  method, warnings }` or `tagged "integrate-1d/non-finite-during-eval"`
  or `tagged "integrate-1d/degenerate-interval"`. Numerical: true.
  `--test` hook reads the manifest and verifies values within
  per-category tolerance.

## Acceptance

- `bun run typecheck` clean.
- `bun test packages/quadrature` green (algebraic-exactness 0..15;
  mutation comments naming ≥2 caught mutations).
- `bun tools/integrate-1d/tool.ts --test` passes (manifest agreement).
- `bun run goldens --tool integrate-1d` writes 30 goldens; oracle
  byte-stable.
- `bun run check` green; `oracle: integrate-1d (30 goldens)` phase
  present.
- README + catalog row in main README + worklog shard.
close_reason: shipped in commit e84c09d (worklog 039); stale in_progress

title: tools/linalg-solve: agent-honest record output (x, residual, condition, growth, warnings)
description: Wrap @workbench/linalg-core's solve as a contract-conforming tool. Input schema: record{A: list<list<float64>>, b: list<float64>}. Output schema (the irresistible part): record{x, residual_norm, b_norm, condition_estimate, growth_factor, method: string, iterations: integer, warnings: list<string>}. Per-tool --test hook proves: matVec(A, x) ≈ b within tol, condition_estimate within 10× of true cond on Hilbert-4.

title: packages/linalg-core: Float64Array Matrix, LU + partial pivoting, solve, Hager condition estimate
description: Pure-TypeScript dense linear algebra substrate. Shape: Matrix = {rows, cols, data: Float64Array} row-major. Public surface: matrixFromRows, matrixToRows, get/set, matVec, vecNorm2, matNorm1, lu, luSolve, solve, hagerOneNormEstimate. Algorithms — LU with partial pivoting (Doolittle, in-place with pivot vector), back/forward substitution, one step of iterative refinement (residual computed in straight float64 — limitation honestly noted), Hager 1-norm estimator for condition number (~4 LU-solves, O(n²) each given the LU). Literate doc-comments throughout (Rule 10) — the file should read like a chapter introducing dense linalg with the references inline. title: cas-core algebraic numbers: Q[α]/(p) primitive + tower composition
description:
Add algebraic-number support to packages/cas-core as the second rung of the cas-core ladder (per docs/cas-core-roadmap.md). Implements Q[α]/(p(α)) for univariate algebraic α, with tower composition for Q[α_1, α_2] = Q[α_1][α_2].

First concrete consumer is sturm-execute (Clifford+T amplitudes need Q[sqrt(2), i]). The implementation should be clean enough that future cyclotomic and arbitrary-algebraic-number extensions follow the same pattern.

REPRESENTATION (per ADR 0008 / cas-core roadmap)
- Chain, not flat: Q ⊂ Q[α_1] ⊂ Q[α_1, α_2] ⊂ ...
- Each level: an element is a Poly<R> in the new generator α_k, reduced mod the level's minimal polynomial p_k(α_k), where R is the previous level's ring.
- Q[sqrt(2), i] specifically: Q[α]/(α²−2) for sqrt(2); Q[sqrt(2)][β]/(β²+1) for i. Q-basis {1, sqrt(2), i, sqrt(2)·i}.

APPROACH
- packages/cas-core/src/algebraic.ts: AlgebraicElement<R>, MinimalPolynomial<R>, AlgebraicRing<R> implementing the Ring interface.
- Operations: add, sub, mul, div (where divisor is invertible — use extended Euclid in the polynomial ring), neg, eq.
- Q[sqrt(2)] and Q[sqrt(2), i] as concrete typed instances exported from cas-core.
- Tests including known-value table (e.g., (1 + sqrt(2))² = 3 + 2sqrt(2); (i)·(sqrt(2)·i) = -sqrt(2); etc.).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- packages/cas-core/src/algebraic.ts exists with the AlgebraicRing<R> implementation.
- Q[sqrt(2)] and Q[sqrt(2), i] exported as named instances.
- ≥20 known-value tests covering ring axioms (associativity, distributivity), the specific Q[sqrt(2), i] structure, and equality/canonical-form properties.
- Mutation-proven: stub the minimal-polynomial reduction in mul, confirm at least 5 tests fail, restore.
- bun run check passes.
- Worklog shard added.
- Cross-references ADR 0008.

DEPENDS ON
- ring-generic refactor issue landed.

BLOCKS

title: cas-core ring-generic refactor: Poly<R> and RatFn<R>
description:
Refactor packages/cas-core to be parametric over a Ring interface. Q stays the v0.1 instance; the refactor preserves all existing behaviour and tests, while opening the door to algebraic numbers, finite fields, and future polynomial-quotient rings.

Touches every cas-core file (~300 LOC churn). Existing 47 unit tests catch breakage. The refactor is load-bearing for the algebraic-numbers issue and everything downstream of it on the cas-core ladder.

APPROACH

- Refactor Rat to implement Ring; export as RAT_RING.
- Refactor Poly: change from hardcoded {coef: Rat, ...} to {coef: T, ring: Ring<T>, ...} (or equivalent typed approach — TS generics over ring instances).

- Refactor expr-bridge to thread the ring through Value <-> Poly translation. Q is the default; algebraic-number bridge follows in a later issue.
- All existing tests pass without changes.

title: ADR 0008: cas-core trajectory + ring-generic refactor
description:
cas-core is currently a v0.1 MVP over Q(x_1,...,x_n). Per docs/cas-core-roadmap.md, its intended trajectory is a real CAS on feature parity with Mathematica/SymPy/Maple/FriCAS. ADR 0008 codifies the next two rungs of that ladder: (1) a ring-generic refactor (Poly<R>, RatFn<R>), and (2) algebraic-number support as the first new ring.

The ring-generic refactor is load-bearing for everything below it on the ladder (algebraic numbers, finite fields, modular arithmetic, future polynomial-quotient rings). It is cheaper now than retrofitting later. Reference: FriCAS's category-of-rings design.

The algebraic-numbers rung represents Q[α]/(p(α)) for univariate algebraic α; tower extensions via composition (Q ⊂ Q[α_1] ⊂ Q[α_1, α_2] ⊂ ...). First concrete consumer is sturm-execute (Clifford+T amplitudes need Q[sqrt(2), i]). Recommended representation: chain, not flat (matches FriCAS; simpler reduction logic).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- docs/adr/0008-cas-core-trajectory-and-ring-generic-refactor.md exists.
- Cross-references PRD §0.1 (the known v0.1 gaps), the cas-core roadmap, ADR 0004 (Schema), and ADR 0006 (where the algebraic-numbers consumer lives).
- Justifies the chain-vs-flat representation choice.
- Commits the project to the multi-year cas-core evolution arc honestly.
- Worklog shard added when the ring-refactor + algebraic-numbers issues land.

title: tools/sturm-equivalent: Clifford+T circuit equivalence over exact algebra
description:
record{lhs, rhs} → record{equal, witness?, side?}. Decide whether two Sturm channels are equivalent. The killer demo for the workbench's exact-symbolic substrate — quantum equivalence checking that doesn't bottom out in floating-point comparison.

Approach (mirrors cas-verify):
- Canonicalise both sides via sturm-simplify.
- For Clifford+T fragments: matrix equivalence over Q[√2, i] using cas-core; equality decided by canonical form match plus algebraic verification of amplitudes.
- For general parametrised circuits: tactical equivalence checking (commutation, controlled-decomposition rules); falls back to numeric comparison with a documented tolerance for non-symbolic cases.
- On inequality: emit a witness — either a difference-IR or a separating measurement basis.

Out-of-scope: circuits beyond the symbolic engine's reach get `tagged "sturm-equivalent/out-of-scope"`.

title: packages/sturm-ir: IR types, schema, well-formedness, traversal
description:
Foundational package consumed by every Sturm tool. Defines the IR Value vocabulary, the schema constructors, well-formedness checks, and traversal helpers.

Surfaces:
- TS types for op nodes: Prepare, Observe, Ry, Rz, Oracle, When, Cases, Discard. Each is a discriminated union member.
- Channel-as-value encoder/decoder (TS shape ↔ canonical Value).
- Schema declarations using S.* constructors from @workbench/protocol — closed union over the op-node vocabulary.
- Well-formedness: wire IDs in scope, controls non-cyclic, dimension consistency, no orphan refs.
- Traversal helpers: visit/transform with controls-stack maintenance during descent into when/cases bodies.

Per the literate-programming axiom in CLAUDE.md, the source files in packages/sturm-ir/src/ are exposition — prose-dominant doc-comments explaining intent and invariants.
design:
Decisions made up-front per ADR 0006:
- Channel encoding: expression-headed "channel" with input_wires, output_wires, body args.
- Op nodes encoded as expression heads matching the op name (prepare, ry, rz, observe, oracle, when, cases, discard).
- Wire IDs are integers scoped to the enclosing channel.
- Dimension descriptor on prepare and on wires; v0.1 only emits "qubit" but the schema accepts the union of all four.

title: Sturm-TS v3.1: reframe P2 as type-level distinction with cq/qc channels
description:
The v3 PRD frames P2 as "boundary is a cast" with prepare and observe as the boundary operations. But prepare and observe ARE channels — the cq channel and qc channel respectively — and sit in the same category as ry, rz, etc. The "boundary as cast" framing inadvertently elevates them in a way that undermines P3 ("op is op"); P2 is properly a *type-level* fact, not a channel-level one.

Updates:
- §1 axiom table P2 row: replace "Boundary is a cast" framing with "Type system separates classical and quantum types; cq channels (prepare, oracle) and qc channels (observe) are the morphisms that cross the type distinction."
- §3.2 prose: clarify that observe is a qc channel — same category as ry, just with different input/output type-shapes.
- Mention that this sharpens P3 — prepare, observe, ry, rz are all uniformly node-shaped in the IR (referenced from ADR 0006).
- Open question Q5 (Classical<T> truthiness) is unaffected.

Spec home: docs/sturm-ts/spec-v3.md (file may not exist yet — issue should also place it under repo control).

title: ADR 0007: distribution-vs-sampling factoring for quantum execution
description:
Quantum execution traditionally bundles "compute the post-circuit state" with "sample measurement outcomes". The workbench's exact-symbolic ethos plus the determinism contract (extended via ADR 0005) make a clean split natural and structurally explicit about Born's rule.

Decisions to record:
- `sturm-execute(ir) → record{distribution, classical_refs}` is fully deterministic; analytic distribution computation, exact-symbolic via cas-core where feasible.
- `sturm-sample(distribution, entropy, shots) → record{samples}` is deterministic given entropy bytes (per ADR 0005).
- Born's rule is therefore structurally explicit in the tool factoring — analytic step + sampling step.

title: ADR 0006: IR-as-Value encoding for Sturm channels
description:
Sturm-TS expresses channels via TS source plus an implicit tracer. For sci-wb integration, the agent-facing protocol object should be the IR Value directly — agents construct the IR; tools transform/execute it. The TS frontend (sturm-trace) becomes one of several possible ways to materialise an IR Value.

Decisions to record:
- Channel encoding: `expression "channel"` carrying input/output wire signatures and a body of op nodes.
- Wire typing: classical/quantum tag + dimension descriptor (qubit, qudit, anyon, boson). v0.1 ships qubit only; the schema accommodates the others additively.
- Closed op-node vocabulary: prepare, observe, ry, rz, oracle, when, cases, discard. No gate names.
- Controls representation: per-op `controls: [WireId]` field — the lowered form of the v3 PRD's whenStack.
- Foreign-pass-through: unknown sub-IR boundary-tagged with the consuming tool's name.
- prepare and observe are channels (cq, qc), not boundary primitives — consistent with P3 op-is-op (see issue for Sturm-TS v3.1 P2 reframe).

title: ADR 0005: externalised entropy and nondeterministic tools in workbench protocol

As Sturm-TS lands and quantum/probabilistic work expands, true randomness becomes necessary (sampling, hardware QPUs, hardware RNG). Decision: externalise entropy as a typed input rather than admit unrestricted nondeterminism.

Decisions to record:
- Default tools remain strictly deterministic (current contract preserved).
- New `nondeterministic: true` annotation in the tool manifest opts in to weakened reproducibility — provenance records the run but does not promise re-derivation.
- One privileged `entropy-source` tool reads OS entropy and is the canonical nondeterministic primitive.
- All other "stochastic" tools take an `entropy` field in input schema and remain deterministic given it.
- Pipe-is-bind: the tools-and-pipes architecture already provides monadic composition; no new value kind required.

title: Tier-1 vocabulary extension: inverse trig + hyperbolics + log-with-base
description:
## Background

Closed-vocabulary surface as of 2026-05-04 (commit f7e0b37):
`+ - * / ^ neg exp sin cos tan log sqrt abs` plus `pi`, `e`. Lives in
`packages/quadrature/src/eval-expr.ts:ADMITTED_HEADS` and
`packages/cas-core/src/diff.ts:DIFF_ADMITTED_HEADS` (matched
deliberately so cas-diff → integrate-1d → optimize composes without
vocabulary mismatches).

A TS expert reaches for `Math.atan`, `Math.tanh`, `Math.log2`
regularly. Their absence is the most-likely-to-bite friction in the
v0.1 surface for any agent doing routine analysis. Each is mechanical
to add (single-argument, maps directly to `Math.*`, has a closed-form
derivative in the existing vocab). Cost is roughly one afternoon for
the whole batch.

## Heads to add (tier 1)

| head | f(x) | f'(x) (in our vocab + new heads) | Math equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asin` | arcsin(x) | `1 / sqrt(1 - x²)` | `Math.asin` |
| `acos` | arccos(x) | `neg(1) / sqrt(1 - x²)` | `Math.acos` |
| `atan` | arctan(x) | `1 / (1 + x²)` | `Math.atan` |
| `sinh` | sinh(x) | `cosh(x)` | `Math.sinh` |
| `cosh` | cosh(x) | `sinh(x)` | `Math.cosh` |
| `tanh` | tanh(x) | `1 - tanh(x)^2` | `Math.tanh` |
| `asinh` | arcsinh(x) | `1 / sqrt(1 + x²)` | `Math.asinh` |
| `acosh` | arccosh(x) | `1 / sqrt(x² - 1)`  (defined for x ≥ 1) | `Math.acosh` |
| `atanh` | arctanh(x) | `1 / (1 - x²)`  (defined for |x| < 1) | `Math.atanh` |
| `log2` | log₂(x) | `1 / (x * log(2))` | `Math.log2` |
| `log10` | log₁₀(x) | `1 / (x * log(10))` | `Math.log10` |

All single-argument; chain rule wraps each as
`d(f(g(x)))/dx = f'(g(x)) · g'(x)`.

`tanh`'s derivative could be `1/cosh(x)^2` — equivalent — but the
`1 - tanh(x)^2` form is the standard textbook expression and avoids
introducing `cosh` evaluation when the original was `tanh`.

## Out of scope (deferred to tier-2)

- Multi-arg `log(base, x)` — variadic shape change, separate proposal.
- `atan2(y, x)` — multi-arg, partial-differentiation design call.
- `min`, `max` — non-smooth at the equality locus; cas-diff would have
  to refuse (or emit subdifferentials honestly).
- `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `trunc`, `sign`, `mod` — non-smooth; eval
  could admit them but cas-diff should refuse. ADR-worthy: should the
  eval-vocab and diff-vocab diverge?
- Special functions (`gamma`, `erf`, `Bessel`, …) — require an actual
  numerical implementation, not just `Math.*` dispatch. Tier-3, file
  separately when motivated.

## Fix

For each head:

1. `packages/quadrature/src/eval-expr.ts`:
   - Append to `ADMITTED_HEADS`.
   - Add a `case "<head>": return Math.<head>(evalNumericExpr(args[0], env));`
     in the `expression` switch.
   - Update the file's documentation block (lines 22–34 list the
     vocabulary verbatim — keep it in lockstep).
2. `packages/cas-core/src/diff.ts`:
   - Append to `DIFF_ADMITTED_HEADS`.
   - Add a `case "<head>":` to `diffExpression` returning the chain-
     rule product (use `mkTimes`, `mkDiv`, `mkPower`, `mkNeg`, `expr`
     helpers and the existing smart constructors).
   - Update the file's documentation block (the rule-table comment
     near the top) so it lists the new rules verbatim.
3. `packages/cas-core/test/diff.test.ts`:
   - Add unit tests for each new head's structural derivative.
   - Add ≥1 FD-corpus probe per new head, with evaluation points
     in the function's natural domain (acosh: x > 1; atanh: |x| < 1;
     log2/log10: x > 0; etc.).
   - The coverage-sanity test will then assert all 24 admitted heads
     appear in the FD corpus — no silent drops.
4. `packages/quadrature/test/eval-expr.test.ts` (if it exists; if not,
   the diff FD-cross-check exercises the eval too):
   - One probe per new head verifying numeric agreement with `Math.*`.

## Documentation lockstep (Law 2)

- `tools/cas-diff/README.md`: extend the rule table.
- `tools/integrate-1d/README.md`: update the closed-vocabulary list.
- `tools/optimize-lbfgs-projected/README.md`: update the closed-vocab list.
- `README.md`: catalog rows for cas-diff, integrate-1d,
  optimize-lbfgs-projected mention the vocab — keep in sync.
- Worklog shard documenting the extension.

## Acceptance

- `bun run check` green: every phase passes including the cas-diff /
  integrate-1d / optimize-lbfgs-projected `--test` and oracle phases.
- `bun test packages/cas-core/test/diff.test.ts` adds ≥11 new tests
  (one per head); coverage-sanity test green with all 24 heads.
- 11 new heads all callable end-to-end through `wb.casDiff`,
  `wb.integrate1d`, `wb.optimizeLbfgsProjected`.
- Three tool READMEs + main README + worklog updated in lockstep.

title: tools/cas-diff: symbolic differentiation over the closed vocabulary
description:
## Background

The friction surfaced during the `min ∫ p(x,a) dx over a ∈ [-1,1]`
demo (scripts/demo-min-integral.ts): integrate-1d and
optimize-lbfgs-projected compose if you can pre-compute the
gradient as an expression — and the natural source of that
expression is symbolic differentiation. cas-simplify exists; the
sister cas-diff does not. Without cas-diff an agent must hand-derive
gradients (or fall back to finite differences, doubling integrate-1d
calls per outer iteration).

This is the cheapest, highest-leverage missing CAS tool given the
two-principles framing (TS-expert + agent-irresistibility).

## Design

### Vocabulary

Closed vocab matches integrate-1d / optimize-lbfgs-projected:
`+ − * / ^ neg exp sin cos tan log sqrt abs` plus constants `pi`, `e`,
plus integer / rational / float64 leaves and symbol variables. (Wider
than cas-simplify's vocab — cas-simplify excludes transcendentals.)

### Differentiation rules (over `var = wrt`):

- atoms: integer/rational/float64 → 0; pi/e → 0
- symbol s: 1 if s.name == wrt.name (and same namespace) else 0
- `+(...)` → `+(da, db, ...)`
- `-(a, b)` → `-(da, db)`; unary `-(a)` → `-(da)`
- `neg(a)` → `neg(da)`
- `*(a, b, ...)` → product rule (n-ary)
- `/(a, b)` → `(da*b - a*db) / b^2`
- `^(a, b)`:
  - b constant in wrt: `b * a^(b-1) * da`        (power rule)
  - a constant in wrt: `a^b * log(a) * db`        (exponential rule)
  - general:           `a^b * (db*log(a) + b*da/a)` (log-chain)
- `exp(a)` → `exp(a) * da`
- `log(a)` → `da / a`
- `sin(a)` → `cos(a) * da`
- `cos(a)` → `neg(sin(a)) * da`
- `tan(a)` → `da / cos(a)^2`
- `sqrt(a)` → `da / (2 * sqrt(a))`
- `abs(a)` → `a/abs(a) * da` (singular at 0; correct on R\{0})

### Boundary discipline

Any subterm head outside the rule table → top-level
`tagged "cas-diff/out-of-scope"` whose payload is the original
input. Binary yes/no for the agent (rather than embedded tagged
sub-nodes that the agent must walk).

### Smart constructors only

Drop `0+x`, `1*x`, `x*0=0`, `x^0=1`, `x^1=x`, `neg(0)=0`,
`neg(neg(x))=x`. No internal cas-simplify call — pipe through
cas-simplify externally if full reduction wanted. Decomposition
discipline (Rule 4 / one tool one operation).

### Library / tool split

- `packages/cas-core/src/diff.ts` — `differentiate(expr, wrt)`
  returning `{kind:"ok",value} | {kind:"out-of-scope",head}`.
- `tools/cas-diff/tool.ts` — wire wrapper, `numerical: false`,
  full provenance.

### Input / output schema

Input: `record { f: <expression>, var: <symbol> }` — `f` mirrors
integrate-1d's field name for cross-tool symmetry.

Output: `<expression>` (record-or-expression Value) on success, or
`tagged "cas-diff/out-of-scope": <original input>` on boundary.

Malformed input (var not a symbol, etc.) → `ToolError` (schema
validation).

## Acceptance

- `bun test packages/cas-core/test/diff.test.ts` green: rule-by-rule
  unit tests + numerical FD cross-check property tests + mutation
  comments naming ≥2 caught mutations.
- `bun tools/cas-diff/tool.ts --test` passes a corpus of ~20
  expressions, asserting numerical agreement (rel ≤ 1e-6) between
  symbolic diff and finite-difference at random points.
- `bun run goldens --tool cas-diff` writes goldens; oracle byte-stable.
- `bun run check` green.
- README + catalog row in main README + worklog shard.
- @workbench/compose typed barrel regenerated.

## Determinism tier

`numerical: false` (default symbolic tier) — output bit-identical
cross-platform forever. Same as cas-simplify. ADR-0015 doesn't apply.

title: ADR-0015: determinism tier — symbolic vs numerical guarantees
description: Forced by the linalg-solve experiment. Splits PRD §6.1's blanket determinism rule into: (a) symbolic tier: same input bytes → bit-identical output bytes across platforms (current rule, unchanged); (b) numerical tier: same input bytes → bit-identical output bytes given (platform, bun_version, libm_version); cross-platform divergence is honest. Includes the per-platform fingerprint format the provenance store carries. Draft AFTER linalg-solve ships AND the property test for single-platform stability runs against multiple Bun versions — those data points are the input to the ADR.

title: linalg-decompose tools (qr, svd, eig) — extension of numerical tier
description: Once linalg-solve is shipped and the determinism-tier ADR drafted, add: tools/linalg-qr (Householder QR with Q optionally explicit), tools/linalg-svd (Golub-Reinsch via bidiagonalization + implicit-shift), tools/linalg-eig (symmetric: Jacobi or QR-iteration; nonsymmetric: deferred). Each gets its own goldens + invariants. Blocked-by: numerical tier landing + agreement on the agent-honest output shape from linalg-solve.

title: Worklog 031: First numerical tier
description: Add docs/worklog/031-first-numerical-tier.md after the work lands. Standard structure (Context → What changed → Why these choices → Frictions → Acceptance → Pointers). Honest about: the determinism question (was Bun's Math.* bit-stable across the development versions used? answer goes here), the wire-encoding cost we measured at n=200, whether the agent-honest record shape survived the runner unchanged, what mutation-proving felt like for numerics, and any surprises with @workbench/protocol's float64FromNumber round-trip.

title: Workbench.lookup(name, input): provenance cache hit by input hash
description: Add lookup(name, input) that canonicalizes + hashes the input, scans the provenance store for a record matching (tool.name, tool.version, inputs[0].hash), and on hit reads the output Value from the store. Returns null on miss. No subprocess work; pure local store lookup. The CAS_STORE layout (provenance/<hh>/<output_hash>.json) means we need a reverse index OR a linear scan — the former is cleaner; the latter is fine for stores up to a few thousand entries. Pick one in the implementation and document the trade-off.
acceptance_criteria: A successful run of mod-pow followed by lookup("mod-pow", sameInput) returns byte-identical Value; different input returns null; tool-version mismatch returns null (different versions are different functions); benches show sub-millisecond hit time on a 1k-entry store.

title: Fluent pipe() API: .through(name, flags?) chaining

title: Fix Sturm-TS spec §8.1 library: H, not, Y derivations under sturm-execute's RY convention
description:
Follow-up to scientist-workbench-4xk (verification confirmed bug under sturm-execute's textbook convention RY(theta) = exp(-i*theta/2 * Y)).

Numerical evidence (scripts/probe-h-equivalence.ts):
- Probe 1 (apply spec H twice, observe): P(r=1)=1.0. Real H·H = I predicts P(r=0)=1.0.
- Probe 2 (spec H, rz(pi), spec H, observe): P(r=0)=1.0. Real H·Z·H = X on |0> predicts P(r=1)=1.0.

Audit of §8.1:

CORRECT under the convention:
- Z(q) := rz(pi). Rz(pi) = diag(-i, i) = -i*Z, so Z up to global phase. OK.
- S(q) := rz(pi/2). Rz(pi/2) = exp(-i*pi/4) * S, so S up to global phase. OK.
- T(q) := rz(pi/4). Rz(pi/4) = exp(-i*pi/8) * T, so T up to global phase. OK.

BUGGY under the convention:
- H(q) := ry(pi/2); ry(pi). Composes to Ry(pi)*Ry(pi/2) = Ry(3pi/2). H has det -1, Ry has det +1; no global phase relates them. Hadamard's Bloch axis is (X+Z)/sqrt(2), no Y-component, so H cannot be expressed in the Ry-only family.
- not(QBool) := ry(pi). Spec comment claims 'X = Ry(pi) up to global phase'; actually Ry(pi) = -i*Y, off from X by Z. In computational-basis bit-flip statistics it acts correctly (golden 05-ry-acts-as-not confirms |0> -> |1>); in coherent compositions with superposition targets it differs from real X.
- Y(q) := rz(pi); ry(pi). State-app order: ry(pi)*rz(pi) = (-iY)*(-iZ) = -YZ = -i*X (since YZ = i*X), so this composes to X up to global phase, NOT Y. The simple correct definition is just Y(q) := ry(pi), since Ry(pi) = -i*Y is Y up to global phase.

DESIGN OPTIONS for the fix:

Option A — ZYZ replacements (coherent equivalence):
  - H(q): rz(pi); ry(pi/2)  (gives -i*H, equal to H up to global phase)
  - not(QBool): rz(pi); ry(pi)  (gives i*X, equal to X up to global phase)
  - Y(q): ry(pi)  (gives -i*Y, equal to Y up to global phase)
  Pros: gates are coherently equivalent to their named referents; works in superposition contexts; phase kickback / Grover / QFT correct.
  Cons: not and H both grow from 1 op to 2 ops; controlled forms (when(c, () => not(t))) become 2-op controlled-rotation sequences; Bell pair example circuit depth doubles.

Option B — keep ry-only, document the caveat:
  - not(QBool): ry(pi). Document 'differs from X by a relative Z; correct for standard-basis bit-flip statistics, not for coherent applications on superposition targets.'
  - H(q): no fix possible (truly cannot be written from ry alone). Must use Option A's form. So this option is partial — H must change regardless.
  - Y(q): ry(pi).
  Pros: minimal circuit-depth impact for not; matches the existing 05-ry-acts-as-not golden's standard-basis interpretation.
  Cons: 'differs from X by Z' is exactly the kind of footgun that breaks phase kickback when an agent reaches for not() inside an oracle.

Option C — change RY convention (NOT recommended):
  Define ry(delta) as a Bloch-rotation by 2*delta, so Ry(pi) corresponds to a Bloch full rotation = -I. Doesn't fix H either. Rejected.

Recommendation: Option A. Pay the circuit-depth cost; library users get gates that are what their names say, no caveats. The implementation cost is small (one extra op per H/not/Y); the readability + correctness benefit is large.

Approach (whichever option chosen):
1. Decide option A or B (or hybrid: A for H, B for not/Y).
2. Update the live spec body? The spec is provenance-preserved verbatim under docs/sturm-ts/spec-v3.md — DO NOT edit the body. Instead either:
   a. Add a docs/sturm-ts/spec-v3-amendments.md with the corrected library derivations, and reference it from the preamble.
   b. Add an §8.1-corrections section to docs/sturm-ts/principles.md (which is the v3.1 source of truth and already supersedes the spec on P2).
3. Update spec-v3.md preamble item 1 to point at the resolution doc.
4. If/when @sturm/library is implemented in the workbench (no current package), use the corrected forms.

Pitfalls:
- The Bell-pair worked example (§13.1) currently uses 'when(a, () => not(b))' with not := ry(pi), which gives correct standard-basis Bell statistics. Under Option A, the example's controlled form changes from cry(a,b,pi) to crz(a,b,pi); cry(a,b,pi) — verify that simplification + execute still produce the same Bell distribution (they should, but worth a sanity probe via scripts/).
- §13.4 phaseKickback comment 'ry(q, Math.PI / 2) // = H, via library' is misleading regardless of which option is chosen. Ry(pi/2) is the correct way to take |0> -> |+>, but it is not 'H' in general. The correction is contextual: 'prepares |+> from |0>' is the honest description.
acceptance_criteria:
Design option (A/B/hybrid) chosen and recorded in this issue's notes.
spec-v3.md preamble item 1 updated to point at the resolution doc.
A docs/sturm-ts/spec-v3-amendments.md (or principles.md addendum) carries the corrected library derivations.
Bell-pair end-to-end probe still produces the textbook Bell distribution under the corrected library forms (run via scripts/, no new tool needed).

title: q0b prerequisite — define tracer rejection rules for non-unitary ops inside when
description:
ADR-0006 admits a 'controls' field only on ry/rz op-nodes (the unitary primitives). Non-unitary ops — observe, cases, discard — have no controls field. The ADR explicitly notes that coherent control on non-unitary ops 'is not well-defined.'

Spec v3 §6 says ops emitted inside a when body carry the whenStack as their controls field, but does not say what happens if observe/cases/discard/prepare appears in a when body. This is a tracer-level invariant sturm-trace (q0b) must enforce before its v0.1.

Approach — decide and document:
1. Which op kinds are forbidden inside a when. At minimum: observe, cases, discard. Open question: is prepare allowed? (Allocates a fresh wire; the wire's |0> amplitude does not depend on the control, so an unconditional prepare inside a when body is harmless.) Recommendation: forbid for v0.1, document, revisit if a use case appears.
2. Error shape. Boundary-tag (tagged 'sturm-trace/invalid-when-body') is the right call per ADR-0003 — the user wrote a syntactically valid but structurally invalid program. ToolError is reserved for malformed input shapes.
3. Defense-in-depth: packages/sturm-ir's wellformed.ts should also catch IR with these violations after the fact, since an agent constructing IR directly could try this. The check walks cases arms recursively and validates that no non-unitary op appears with controls in scope.

Pitfall: do not relax the rule by adding controls fields to observe/cases/discard. ADR-0006's rationale (coherent control on non-unitary ops is ill-defined) is load-bearing.
acceptance_criteria:
Decision documented in q0b's notes (forbidden ops, error shape).
packages/sturm-ir/src/wellformed.ts updated to catch the violations structurally (independent of any tracer).
Tests cover at least one rejection path per forbidden op.

title: Verify Sturm-TS spec §8.1 library Y-axis derivations against sturm-execute's convention
description:
Spec docs/sturm-ts/spec-v3.md §8.1 defines library gates from the three primitives. Two derivations look suspect under sturm-execute's textbook convention (tools/sturm-execute/tool.ts:408 — RY(theta) = [[cos(theta/2), -sin(theta/2)], [sin(theta/2), cos(theta/2)]]):

- not(QBool) ::= ry(pi). Comment claims 'X = Ry(pi) up to global phase.' Under the textbook convention Ry(pi) = [[0,-1],[1,0]] = -i*Y, which differs from X by a Z (X = Z*Ry(pi)), not by a global phase.
- H(q) ::= ry(pi/2); ry(pi). Body composes (source-order = state-application-order) to Ry(pi)*Ry(pi/2) = Ry(3pi/2). H has det -1; Ry(3pi/2) has det +1; no phase factor relates them. H's Bloch axis is (X+Z)/sqrt(2) which has no Y-component, so H cannot be expressed in the Ry-only family.

If correct as written, the v0.1 library would silently produce wrong amplitudes for any Hadamard-using algorithm (Grover, QFT, Deutsch-Jozsa, Bernstein-Vazirani, ...). BUT — this kind of 'is it a phase or not' question has tripped agents looking at Sturm.jl analogues before, and may reflect a convention difference (e.g. Sturm.jl might define ry as a 2x-Bloch-rotation, or the library may carry an implicit standard-basis-only caveat) rather than a derivation bug. Numerical run is the source of truth.

Approach — drive sturm-execute on two probes that distinguish real H from Ry(3pi/2):

Probe 1 — H*H = I sanity check (apply spec H twice):
  IR sequence: prepare(0); ry(pi/2); ry(pi); ry(pi/2); ry(pi); observe(r)
  Real H semantics: H*H = I, so P(r=0) = 1.
  Spec-library semantics: Ry(pi/2)+Ry(pi)+Ry(pi/2)+Ry(pi) fuses to Ry(3pi) = i*Y, so |0> maps to -|1>, so P(r=1) = 1.

Probe 2 — H*Z*H = X (apply spec H, Z, spec H):
  IR sequence: prepare(0); ry(pi/2); ry(pi); rz(pi); ry(pi/2); ry(pi); observe(r)
  Real H semantics: H*Z*H = X applied to |0>, so P(r=1) = 1.
  Spec-library semantics: composes to -i*Z applied to |0>, so P(r=0) = 1.

Both probes predict opposite outcomes between real-H and spec-library, so one run resolves it.

Decide:
- If empirically distinguishable from real H: spec library has a derivation bug. Propose ZYZ Euler form (e.g. H = Rz(pi/2)*Ry(pi/2)*Rz(pi/2) up to global phase), file follow-up fix issue, update spec-v3.md preamble to reflect resolved status.
- If empirically equivalent to real H: I have misread the convention. Document the convention difference in spec-v3.md and principles.md, close as 'not a bug.'

Pitfalls:
- Bell-pair / GHZ goldens use only standard-basis prep + standard-basis measurement, which mask the Ry(pi) vs X relative-phase difference. Probes above are designed to expose the difference via composition.
- sturm-simplify will fuse adjacent same-axis ry's. That is fine — the fused angle still distinguishes (Ry(3pi) is not I).
acceptance_criteria:
Both probe IRs run through tools/sturm-execute; outputs recorded in issue notes.
Decision recorded in issue: bug -> file fix issue + update spec-v3.md preamble; not-bug -> document convention difference, close as 'not a bug.'
spec-v3.md preamble open-issue note for §8.1 updated to reflect resolution.
close_reason: Verified empirically via scripts/probe-h-equivalence.ts: spec §8.1 H derivation produces Ry(3pi/2), not Hadamard, under sturm-execute's textbook RY convention. Probe 1 (H*H): P(r=1)=1.0 (real H predicts P(r=0)=1.0). Probe 2 (HZH): P(r=0)=1.0 (real H predicts P(r=1)=1.0). Both probes confirm. Audit also flagged not(QBool) (off from X by Z) and Y(q) (composes to X, not Y) as bugs; Z/S/T are correct. Fix issue scientist-workbench-1td filed with design options (Option A: ZYZ replacements; Option B: keep ry-only with documented caveat for not/Y but H must change). spec-v3.md preamble updated to reflect verified-bug-confirmed status.

title: sturm-execute exact-symbolic path: Q[√2,i] amplitudes with Q[√2]-rational probabilities
description:
Follow-up to tkx (v0.1 sturm-execute ships float64-only). The exact path was deferred because individual measurement probabilities for the restricted gate set {prepare(0|1|1/2), ry(kπ/2), rz(kπ/2)} land in Q[√2], not Q. Concrete counterexample: ry(π/2)·CRy(π/2)·ry(π/2) on |00⟩ produces amps with mixed Q+√2·i components, and Prob(wire_0=0)=1/2−√2/4 (irrational). The unitarity invariant Σ|amp|²=1 still holds rationally, but per-outcome marginals don't.

Design questions to resolve before this lands:
1. Probability shape: extend schema to admit Q[√2]-rational probabilities? Or convert to float64 and label precision='exact-amps-float-prob'? Or restrict scope further (only circuits where outcome probabilities are provably Q-rational)?
2. Renormalisation strategy after observe: don't renormalise (carry sub-normalised amps; branch probability = Σ|amp|²) is the cleanest with our gate set since renormalisation factors √Prob can be irrational.
3. Recogniser API: cas-simplify the angle, then a pattern-matcher over the canonical form for k·π/2 multiples. Falls back to float64 path if any angle/prob doesn't recognise.

Implementation sketch:
- Use packages/cas-core's Q_SQRT2_I as the amplitude ring.
- ComplexRing<Amp,Real> abstraction over (Q[√2,i], Q[√2]) for exact and ({re,im}, number) for float64.
- Output: extend distributionOutcomeSchema with an 'exact-q-sqrt2' probability variant (record{a, b} encoding a + b√2)?

Pre-conditions: tkx (sturm-execute float64) closed; sturm-equivalent (564) close to landing so we know what shape exact equivalence checks need.

title: tools/sturm-controlled: channel combinators (controlled, then, tensor)
description:
A small group of channel-on-channel transformations that give point-free composition at the Value level. Together with sturm-qecc-wrap and sturm-bennett-oracle, these are the higher-order operators that make the channel category visible at the agent layer.

Tools (one tool dir per combinator, or a single tool dispatching on a flag — TBD in design):
- `controlled(c, f)`: take a control wire and a channel; emit a channel where every op in f's body carries c on its `controls` field.
- `then(f, g)`: sequential composition. Output wires of f wired into input wires of g; signatures must match.
- `tensor(f, g)`: parallel composition. Produces a channel whose wires are the disjoint union of f's and g's.

Tool invariants: the categorical laws — associativity of `then`, identity laws, monoidal-functor laws for `tensor`.
design: Open: one tool per combinator vs. one tool with a mode flag. The CLAUDE.md guidance "Flags that change the type of the output should be different tools" suggests separate tools, since `controlled` consumes a channel + control wire while `then` consumes two channels. Default to separate tools; revisit if redundancy in scaffolding is significant.
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/sturm-controlled/, tools/sturm-then/, tools/sturm-tensor/ each conform to the 7-artefact contract — OR a unified tools/sturm-compose/ if design favours one tool with mode flag.
- ≥10 examples per tool covering identity, associativity, edge cases (empty body, mismatched signatures with tagged failure).
- Property tests for the categorical laws.
- Main README.md catalog rows.
close_reason: Three sibling tools shipped: sturm-controlled (19 goldens, control-stamping + wire-conflict + non-unitary boundary tags), sturm-then (14 goldens, signature-matching + wire-id offset rename + associativity property), sturm-tensor (13 goldens, monoidal product with shift-by-max+1 rename + identity laws + associativity, total). All conform to the 7-artefact contract; categorical-law property tests pass in --test hooks. Main README catalog rows added; demo-scope.sh demo 13 (sturm-then prepare∘observe → sturm-execute end-to-end) verifies the composition works through the pipeline. bun run check: 29 phases pass, 0 failed. Classical-ref renaming is a known v0.1 limitation (see sturm-tensor README) — tensoring two channels that bind the same ref produces a duplicate-binding flaw caught by checkWellFormed; future work could add a sturm-rename-refs tool.

title: tools/sturm-qecc-wrap: channel → encoded channel (P6 realisation)
description:
record{channel, code} → channel. The workbench realisation of P6: QECC is a channel-on-channel transformation that preserves wire-shape signatures.

Approach:
- code is a record naming a code (e.g., "steane", "surface-d3", "repetition-3") plus parameters.
- Wrap each logical wire of the input channel with encode/decode IR substitutions, threading ancilla wires through.
- The output channel has the same input/output wire signature as the input — that's the P6 invariant, captured as a tool invariant.

v0.2 scope: at minimum the repetition code (3-qubit bit-flip / phase-flip). Steane and surface deferred.
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/sturm-qecc-wrap/{tool.ts, package.json, README.md, goldens.spec.ts, goldens/} per the 7-artefact contract.
- ≥10 examples: identity-on-encoded-Bell, single-qubit-error-corrected, syndrome-extraction.
- P6 invariant property test: input.signature === output.signature (wire shape preservation).
- Round-trip: encode + decode = identity (logical) up to ancilla.
- Main README.md catalog row.

title: tools/sturm-bennett-oracle: classical-reversible function → IR oracle node
description:
record{fn_description, arg_types} → IR oracle node. Compiles a classical reversible function into an IR oracle node that the simulator and other Sturm tools can consume.

The natural integration with the existing workbench: classical primitives (mod-pow, mod-inv, polynomial evaluation via cas-core) are already content-addressed and exact. Bennett's oracle lift is the bridge from "exact classical" to "reversible quantum oracle" — and it's the route to algorithms like Shor.

Approach:
- fn_description as an expression tree describing the classical computation (could reference workbench tools by name, or carry a literal arithmetic expression).
- Compilation: synthesise a reversible circuit (bit-arithmetic or modular-arithmetic primitives) that computes f(x) on a register pair (x, ancillae) → (x, f(x)).
- arg_types declares the bit-widths and dimensions of input wires.
- Output is a single IR oracle node with `circuit: ReversibleCircuit, in_wires, out_wires` per the v3 PRD's IR vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/sturm-bennett-oracle/{tool.ts, package.json, README.md, goldens.spec.ts, goldens/} per the 7-artefact contract.
- ≥10 examples: bit AND/OR/XOR, integer add, modular-add, modular-multiply, modular-pow (composing mod-core), polynomial evaluation.
- Reversibility property test: every emitted circuit is a permutation on the joint state.
- Main README.md catalog row.

title: tools/sturm-trace: TS source → IR (TypeScript frontend)
description:
record{source, entry?} → IR. Compiles a TS Sturm program (the @sturm/core + @sturm/library frontend per the v3 PRD) and runs the implicit tracer in a sandboxed Bun subprocess to produce the IR.

Approach:
- Use spawnBun (per ADR 0001) to run the user source in a tracer-enabled context.
- The tracer's module-level state is contained inside the subprocess; outside, the tool's behaviour is purely a function of (source bytes, entry name).
- Deterministic across same source bytes — the v3 PRD's STURM_CHECK_DETERMINISM=1 mode is on by default in this tool.
- Boundary failures: source compile errors emit `tagged "sturm-trace/parse-error"`; tracer-stage errors (e.g., closures over mutable state) emit `tagged "sturm-trace/non-pure-trace"`.

Out of scope for v0.2: nested run() (per the v3 PRD; defer to future AsyncLocalStorage work).
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/sturm-trace/{tool.ts, package.json, README.md, goldens.spec.ts, goldens/} per the 7-artefact contract.
- ≥10 examples: Bell pair, GHZ, phase kickback, parametrised circuit, classical-branch via cases.
- Determinism property test: trace twice, IR identical.
- Round-trip with sturm-execute: traced IR + execute matches expected distribution.
- Main README.md catalog row.
notes:
Bennett-TS not yet ported (no @bennett/core in this ecosystem). v3 spec §10 oracle bridge depends on it; §13.4 (phase kickback) and §13.5 (Shor) examples are correspondingly unrunnable until Bennett-TS lands. q0b v0.1 must boundary-fail on user code that calls oracle() — emit tagged 'sturm-trace/bennett-missing' with a clear message and a reference to the missing dependency.

Tracer-time rejection rules for non-unitary ops inside when (observe/cases/discard) are tracked separately in scientist-workbench-r40 and are a hard prerequisite — needs to be settled before q0b's tracer code lands.

The user-facing run() ergonomic surface (Spec §5.2 RunResult<O> shape) is also under-specified post ADR-0007 (distribution-vs-sampling); tracked in scientist-workbench-4iw. q0b itself only emits IR; the Run reconstruction is downstream and not blocking for q0b v0.1.

title: tools/sturm-sample: distribution + entropy → samples (deterministic given entropy)
description:
record{distribution, entropy, shots} → record{samples, classical_resolutions}. Apply Born's rule numerically against an entropy stream; resolve Classical refs against the sampled bitstring.

Deterministic given entropy bytes. Same distribution + same entropy ⟹ same samples. The randomness of measurement is reified as a pure function of the seed.

Approach:
- Treat the entropy bytes as a stream of uniform-[0,1) draws (e.g., 8 bytes per draw).
- For each shot: walk the distribution's CDF to pick an outcome.
- Resolve Classical refs in the IR's classical_refs map using the sampled outcome.
- Output: record{samples: list<bitstring>, classical_resolutions: map<ref, list<value>>, entropy_consumed: integer (bytes)}.
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/sturm-sample/{tool.ts, package.json, README.md, goldens.spec.ts, goldens/} per the 7-artefact contract.
- ≥10 examples covering: trivial-distribution, Bell-pair correlation, GHZ all-correlated, and explicit entropy-determinism cases.
- Statistical property test: large-shot distributions converge to the input distribution within tolerance.
- Determinism property test: same (distribution, entropy) ⟹ same samples.
- Main README.md catalog row.

title: oracle: throw rather than process.exit on golden failure
description:
tools/oracle/tool.ts:182-186 calls process.exit(1) from inside fn after writing canonical bytes directly to stdout. This bypasses runTool'\''s normal flow — no provenance write happens for partial-pass records — and is inconsistent with how every other tool handles failure (throw ToolError, runTool catches and exits).

Refactor so fn throws a ToolError carrying the failed-results record as detail. Have runTool grow a path for ToolError-with-output (or have oracle emit a record { failed, ... } as its happy path output and let the user decide; CI can test --provenance-of on the result hash).

title: Encapsulate NTT caches in an NTTContext
description:
packages/mod-core/src/ntt.ts has three module-level mutable Maps: POW2_TWIDDLE_CACHE (line 84), BLUESTEIN_CACHE (line 153), POW2_INV_N_MONT_CACHE (line 207). Three problems:

1. Unbounded — a fuzz test with arbitrary n leaks memory.
2. Process-global — currently safe because modulus is frozen, but a future generalisation to other NTT-friendly primes will collide on cache keys.
3. Make nttCore non-pure: timings depend on what came before. Outputs are still deterministic but it'\''s a footgun worth removing.

Fix: NTTContext class owning the caches, created once per modulus, threaded through nttCore. Deprecate the module-level Maps.
acceptance_criteria: NTTContext type exists; nttCore takes (x, opts, ctx?) with a default context; module-level Maps removed or marked private to the default ctx; tests pass

title: Document mmul invariants in mod-core/ntt.ts
description:
packages/mod-core/src/ntt.ts:31-64 (mmul) is correct hand-rolled Montgomery REDC but unreviewable by anyone not already deep in the algorithm. Two specific additions:

1. Top-of-function paragraph: '\''input a, b ∈ [0, 2^32); output is a·b·R⁻¹ mod p ∈ [0, p) where R = 2^32. Uses 16-bit limb partial products to keep every intermediate < 2^32 and out of BigInt.'\''
2. Line-by-line algebra tie-back, especially line 45 (Math.imul(tLo | 0, P_INV) >>> 0): '\''the n'\'' multiplication; we keep only the low 32 bits because the upper bits are scaled away by R in the next step.'\''

CLAUDE.md literate-programming principle is being honoured elsewhere (spawn.ts, json-bridge); ntt.ts is the file most in need of catching up.
acceptance_criteria: mmul has a header invariant block + line-by-line algebra annotations; a fresh reader can verify the REDC by reading top to bottom

title: Cache tool metadata so registry doesn't spawn 4× per tool
description:
packages/contract/src/registry.ts:53-58 (describeTool) shells out for --version, --schema, --examples, --invariants for every tool. With 50 tools that'\''s 200 spawns per registry-list call.

Two paths:
1. Intermediate: have generate-goldens.ts (or a new scripts/build-metadata.ts) emit tools/<name>/metadata.json on every check; registry reads from disk.
2. Right answer: blocked on issue scientist-workbench-yth (split defineTool from runTool). Registry imports the def directly from tool.ts via the workspace, no spawn at all.

Choose path 2 if scientist-workbench-yth lands first; otherwise path 1 as a stopgap.

title: runTool: hashCanonicalBytes instead of double-canonicalize
description:
packages/contract/src/runner.ts:219, 224, 225. canonicalize(output) is computed for stdout, then hash(output) is called for the provenance record — but hash() (packages/protocol/src/hash.ts:8-10) calls canonicalize() internally. The output value is canonicalised twice per run.

Plumb outBytes once: const outBytes = canonicalize(output); process.stdout.write(outBytes); const outputHash = hashCanonicalBytes(outBytes);. hashCanonicalBytes already exists at hash.ts:12.

title: canonicalize: typed switch over Value.kind, drop duck-typing
description:
packages/protocol/src/canonical.ts:8-44 (encodeAny) walks unknown rather than narrowing on Value. Half the function is defensive branches (Array.isArray, typeof number, x===null, typeof bigint) that cannot fire on a validated Value input. parse() validates upstream, so the encoder doesn'\''t need to defend against arbitrary objects.

Rewrite as an exhaustive switch on v.kind. Shorter (~20 lines), faster, and noFallthroughCasesInSwitch (already enabled in tsconfig.json:11) gives compile-time coverage. Keep a separate validateAndCanonicalize for the rare callers that genuinely have unknown input.
acceptance_criteria: encodeAny replaced by a typed Value switch; round-trip property test still passes; benchmarks (if any) flat or improved

title: Dedupe INT_RE and F64_BITS_RE across protocol
description:
Same regexes in packages/protocol/src/kinds.ts:103-104 and packages/protocol/src/validate.ts:9-10. Both load-bearing — they must agree forever. Today they happen to; they will drift.

Hoist to one constants module within the protocol package and import from both call sites.

title: Hoist gcdBigInt to a shared protocol util
description:
gcdBigInt is defined three times with identical bodies: packages/protocol/src/kinds.ts:106-115, packages/protocol/src/validate.ts:178-187, packages/cas-core/src/rat.ts:9-18.

Move to a single canonical location (likely packages/protocol/src/numerics.ts or similar internal module) and import from the three call sites. Either export from @workbench/protocol or keep package-private and have cas-core re-implement consciously — but not by accident.
