title: F6: mixed Value-construction styles (record({...}) vs raw object literals)
description:
Symptom: codebase mixes record({...})/int(...)/list(...) helpers (in cas-simplify, etc.) with raw {kind:..., fields:...} object literals (notably in oracle, scripts, some tests). Both work but both being canonical means a fresh reader can't tell which is convention.

Fix: settle on the helpers as the canonical construction path in tool/test/script code. Reserve raw literals for protocol internals. Add a quick eslint or grep-based check in scripts/check.ts that flags raw 'kind:' literals outside packages/protocol.
notes: Resolved 2026-04-28. Migrated cas-simplify/goldens.spec.ts (str/list helpers) and scripts/check.ts (record/str/canonicalize helpers) off raw {kind:...} literals. Added a 'convention: raw kind-literals' phase to scripts/check.ts that greps for the antipattern outside an allowlist (packages/protocol, packages/contract/src/runner.ts, packages/json-bridge/src, *.test.ts, check.ts itself). Currently passes with 0 drift sites; warning-only for now (will flip to hard-fail once the convention is well-established).

title: F4: example-count target (≥10) clashes with structure-driven minimums
description:
Symptom: PRD §6.1 / README require ≥10 examples per tool. For mod-pow I padded with NTT-relevant exponents to hit 12; for ntt the natural set was ~11 (one per code-path branch + edge cases). The literal count requirement pushes against the structural quality goal.

Fix: revise PRD §6.1 to state: 'one example per code-path branch + edge cases, ≥10 once done.' For v0.1 prototypes the soft floor is 'every code-path branch covered.' Document in README's 'writing a new tool' section.
notes: Resolved 2026-04-28. README §The contract artefact 3 reframed: 'soft floor: one example per code-path branch + edge cases; ≥10 done; ≥30 v1-complete.' Structure-driven coverage now explicitly the priority over the literal count.

title: tools/linalg-equiv: numerical analogue of cas-verify (equal-within-tolerance)
description: Numerical analogue of cas-verify. Decides whether two SolveResult records (or, generally, two records of the same shape with float64 leaves) are equal-within-tolerance. Schema: input record{lhs, rhs, rtol?, atol?}; output record{equal: boolean, max_abs_diff: float64, max_rel_diff: float64, where?: string}. Boundary categories per ADR-0003: malformed inputs (different shapes, non-finite leaves) raise ToolError; equality decisions are routine non-success per the record-with-flag pattern. Implementation rides @workbench/linalg-core's Float64Array machinery. Forces ADR-0015's "cross-platform numerical evidence" framing into a concrete tool: cross-platform records that pass linalg-equiv are evidence of agreement up to tolerance even when output_hashes differ. Filed as a follow-up to ADR-0015 — independent of the determinism-tier ADR landing.

title: Cross-arch stability measurement (linux-x86_64 vs darwin-aarch64)
description: Cross-architecture stability measurement: run scripts/measure-cross-bun-stability.ts on darwin-aarch64 (Apple Silicon) and on linux-aarch64 if available; diff against the linux-x86_64 corpus committed under docs/data/cross-bun-stability/. Goal: calibrate whether ADR-0015's PlatformRecord needs only {arch, os, runtime} or also fields that distinguish JSC builds within an arch+os pair. Without this data, ADR-0015 documents the linux-x86_64 single-platform window only and defers the arch-axis fingerprint shape. Acceptance: a third TSV under docs/data/cross-bun-stability/, plus a 1-paragraph addendum in the README naming which goldens diverge (if any) and which fields of PlatformRecord move the bits.

title: cas-to-latex — symbolic-vis experiment (companion to numerics)
description: docs/numerics-and-vis-2026-04-29.md §5.2. Consume an expression Value, emit a string of LaTeX. Output is a primitive (string), no blob/visual machinery needed. Tests whether 'visual: true' annotation is needed for symbolic vis (likely not). Independent of the numerical tier; could ship in parallel. Filed now so the §5 experiment portfolio is tracked as a unit.

title: bun:ffi BLAS path for n > 200 dense linalg (deferred)
description: When n > 200 stops being acceptable in pure TS, the path of least resistance is bun:ffi to OpenBLAS / LAPACK on the local install. Forces: cross-platform determinism question (libm + BLAS reduction order), license matrix expansion (BSD-licensed BLAS is fine for AGPL parent), the 'same algorithm, two backends' question (do we ship two tools or one tool with --backend flag? PRD §6.1's 'few flags, all orthogonal' suggests two tools). Defer until a workload demands it.

title: Blob-by-hash convention experiment (forced when numerics demands n > 200)
description: docs/numerics-and-vis-2026-04-29.md §3.1 + §5.1. Add /blobs/<hh>/<hash>.bin sibling slot. Tools opt into descriptor shape: record{blob_hash, dtype: 'float64', shape: list<integer>, layout: 'row-major'}. First customer: linalg-solve-large (n > 200), or oracle goldens that have outgrown inline JSON. NOT a new value-protocol kind — record convention only. Defer until a real workload demands it (this bead is the placeholder).

title: Workbench.runMemoized(): lookup-or-run convenience wrapper
description: Try lookup(); on miss, fall through to run() (which already writes provenance, so the next call hits the cache). One-line wrapper but the ergonomic surface is the win: agents mark hot paths as memoizable without thinking about cache lifecycle. Document the determinism precondition: memoization is unsafe for tools with nondeterministic=true (entropy-source) — runMemoized must refuse those by checking def.nondeterministic and falling through to run() unconditionally with a warning, or rejecting at lookup time. Pick which in the impl.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated runMemoized calls show: first call writes to disk, second call short-circuits to cache, both return byte-identical Value; calling runMemoized on entropy-source either warns + bypasses cache OR throws (impl picks one and worklog notes); doc note in compose README explains the determinism precondition.

title: Standard --verbose / --quiet flags across all tools
description: ADR-0011 unblocks this. Add --verbose and --quiet to the standard flag table in packages/contract/src/runner.ts STANDARD_FLAGS so every tool acquires them uniformly. Tools opt in to checking flags.verbose / flags.quiet where it matters (oracle already has its own --verbose; merge with the standard one). The standard set should propagate consistent stderr-progress conventions across the workbench rather than each tool inventing its own knob. Out of scope for the rej acceptance criterion, filed as a follow-up.

title: Design run() ergonomic surface bridging q0b output to sturm-execute + sturm-sample
description:
Spec v3 §5.2 defines run<F>(f, opts): Promise<RunResult<F>> returning {output: ResolveClassical<ReturnType<F>>, measurements, shots}. This shape predates ADR-0007's distribution-vs-sampling split — the workbench factored execution into sturm-execute (analytic distribution) and sturm-sample (per-shot resolutions given entropy).

q0b (sturm-trace) emits only IR. A user-facing run() needs additional plumbing: take q0b's IR output, pipe through sturm-execute, optionally pipe through sturm-sample, then reconstruct RunResult<O> by mapping the IR's classical_ref strings back to the user's Classical<T> brand handles (correspondence established at trace time).

Approach — decide and document:
1. Where the bridge lives:
   a. A new tool sturm-run that composes sturm-trace | sturm-execute | sturm-sample into a single invocation.
   b. A user-facing TS function run() exported from packages/sturm-trace-runtime/ (the runtime package q0b will spawn) that does the composition in-process.
   c. Leave it to userland — agents compose by-pipe with no convenience wrapper.
2. How RunResult<O>.measurements: Map<ClassicalRef, boolean> is reconstructed from sturm-sample's samples: list<record> output. The mapping between TS-side Classical<T> brand handles and IR-side classical_ref strings is established at trace time.
3. Whether this is q0b-blocking or a follow-up.

This issue is q0b-adjacent but not strictly required for q0b's 'trace-only' v0.1. Filed separately to surface the design question before q0b implementation begins; may be folded into q0b's body or absorbed into the runtime package issue once the call is made.
acceptance_criteria:
Decision recorded (option a/b/c with justification).
If a or b chosen: implementation issue filed.
spec-v3.md preamble open-issue note for run() updated to reflect resolution.

title: Epic: hardware backend bridges (qpu-execute-* tools)
description:
Tracking issue for Phase-3 work: bridges to actual quantum hardware (IBM Quantum, AWS Braket, IonQ, etc.). Deferred until v0.2 stabilises.

Each backend is its own tool: `qpu-execute-<backend>(ir, job-token, ...) → record{measurements, ...}`.

Approach:
- Annotated `nondeterministic: true` per ADR 0005 — hardware execution is the canonical "world-fact" tool.
- Each backend gets its own ADR documenting API shape, auth, error handling, and the cost/credentials/rate-limit model.
- IR is lowered to backend-native ops via sturm-lower (Phase-3 partner tool, separate issue when scoped).
- Job submission and result fetching may need to be split across two tools if backends are async-only.

Pre-requisites: ADR 0005 entropy/nondeterminism, sturm-execute, sturm-sample, sturm-trace.
acceptance_criteria:
This is an epic / tracking issue. Acceptance is "scope decided, sub-issues filed" rather than "implementation complete". Sub-issues to file when started:
- ADR per backend (auth, API, error model, rate-limit handling).
- Tool per backend.
- Possible companion sturm-lower tool for backend-specific IR lowering.

title: expr-parse self-test: compare via canonicalize, not JSON.stringify
description:
tools/expr-parse/tool.ts:309-312 round-trips through parseValue(JSON.stringify(...)) to compare two values structurally. This works only because both sides happen to be re-parsed from JSON; under any non-canonical key ordering it would silently break.

Use canonicalize(a) === canonicalize(b) — that'\''s exactly what the protocol guarantees structural equality means.
acceptance_criteria: self-test in expr-parse uses canonicalize for the equality check; tests still pass
close_reason: Fixed incidentally during the Schema landing (worklog 008). runner.ts now uses hashCanonicalBytes(outBytes) and provenanceToValue(rec); invariantToValue uses bool(); expr-parse self-test compares via canonicalize.

title: expr-parse: avoid string += in number/identifier accumulators
description:
tools/expr-parse/tool.ts:143-182 (parseNumber) accumulates digits via intPart += this.advance() / fracPart += this.advance() / denPart += this.advance(). Same pattern in parseIdentifier (184-188).

V8 worst case is O(n²) on these shapes. Use start-index + slice: let start = this.pos; while (...) this.pos++; const intPart = this.src.slice(start, this.pos).
acceptance_criteria: parseNumber and parseIdentifier use slice rather than += accumulation; existing tests and goldens pass

title: Dedupe cas-verify try/catch with tryToRatFn helper
acceptance_criteria: verify.ts has no duplicated try/catch; behaviour bytes-identical on existing tests and goldens

title: Verify cas-simplify recurseChildren collapse fixture
description:
packages/cas-core/src/simplify.ts:23-44 (recurseChildren) recursively simplifies children of an out-of-scope expression — eg. sin(1+1) should produce tagged(simplify/oos, sin(2)). The example exists in tools/cas-simplify/tool.ts:67-71 and the matching golden, but there is no dedicated test for the edge case where simplifying a child collapses something that was structurally complex into a literal.

Add a unit test asserting that arithmetic *inside* an out-of-scope head reduces while the wrap is preserved verbatim. Cover at least: sin(1+1), sin(x+x), f(g(2*3)).
acceptance_criteria: packages/cas-core/test (or new test file) exercises recurseChildren collapse for at least three nested cases; passes under bun test

title: Decide fpInv vs Fermat in NTT plan-build
description:
packages/mod-core/src/ntt.ts:74-80 (fpInv) calls modInv (extended Euclid, generic for any modulus) even though p = 998244353 is prime. Fermat'\''s little theorem (a^(p-2) mod p) is simpler and removes the dependency on the ModInvResult shape (modular.ts:31-38) inside the NTT core.

Options: (a) inline Fermat in fpInv and keep the dependency local; (b) keep the modInv call and document why (consistency with the modular package). Either is fine — choose and comment.
acceptance_criteria: Either fpInv uses Fermat with a one-line comment, or the modInv call has a comment explaining the deliberate choice

title: ADR pinning Exp representation and migration to dense vectors
description:
packages/cas-core/src/poly.ts:33-77 uses Exp = ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, number]>, with expKey = JSON.stringify(e) as the Map key. polyMul (poly.ts:113-132) is O(|a|×|b|) with a JSON serialisation per key access. Fine for (x+1)(x-1); will collapse on Buchberger over a 5-variable system, polynomial GCD, or factoring — anything one would actually use a CAS for.

Don'\''t fix now. File ADR-0005 pinning the current representation as a known wart with the planned migration: either Map<varName, exponent> per monomial with precomputed degVec, or fixed-variable-order Uint32Array exponent vectors (what every serious CAS uses). Decision triggers when cas-reduce or Gröbner work begins.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-0005 filed, references current poly.ts code, names the trigger for migration, lists candidate representations with tradeoffs

title: runTool --provenance-of: reuse provenanceToValue helper
description:
packages/contract/src/runner.ts:179-197 rebuilds the provenance record by hand (constructs the flagFields/inputs/output_hash/tool record manually). packages/contract/src/provenance.ts:24-33 already has provenanceToValue doing the same thing.

Two implementations of the same transform will drift. Collapse to one path: have the --provenance-of branch call provenanceToValue and emit the canonical bytes.
acceptance_criteria: runner.ts --provenance-of branch is one call to provenanceToValue + writeOut; bytes-identical to current output
close_reason: Fixed incidentally during the Schema landing (worklog 008). runner.ts now uses hashCanonicalBytes(outBytes) and provenanceToValue(rec); invariantToValue uses bool(); expr-parse self-test compares via canonicalize.

title: Lazy path reconstruction in protocol error paths
description:
canonical.ts and validate.ts allocate and spread path arrays on every recursive call: [...path, key] at canonical.ts:17, 27 and validate.ts:115, 126, 138, 144. The path is only consumed when an error throws — never on the happy path.

Two cleaner shapes: (a) carry a parent link (linked list) and reconstruct path on throw; (b) carry a depth counter + a reusable scratch buffer. Either way, eliminate per-recursion allocation.
acceptance_criteria: No path-array allocation on the happy path; ProtocolError messages still include the dotted path on failure; existing tests pass

title: encodeString: avoid quadratic string concat
description:
packages/protocol/src/canonical.ts:46-62. Loop builds the result with out += s.charAt(i) for every character. V8 has worst-case O(n²) behaviour for some string-concat shapes; a hot-path encoder for canonical bytes should not be exposed to it.

Replace with parts.push(...) + parts.join('\'''\''), or use String.prototype.replace over the seven escape characters in a single pass.
acceptance_criteria: encodeString uses a non-quadratic strategy; round-trip test passes; spot-benchmark on a 100KB string shows linear scaling

title: F9: TDD discipline doc — distinguish 'spec from scratch' from 'port and verify'
description:
Symptom: README's 'writing a new tool' section assumes pure RED→GREEN. When porting a known-good algorithm (as we did with NTT), the cycle is: write impl, write tests, mutation-prove tests catch regressions. Both are valid TDD-shaped workflows but the discipline is different.

Fix: add a section to README (or a new docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) describing both flows: 'Port and verify' vs 'Spec from scratch.' Include the mutation-prove technique (deliberately break the impl, confirm tests go RED, restore).
notes: Resolved 2026-04-28. CLAUDE.md adds 'Two TDD shapes — both valid': spec-from-scratch (classic RED→GREEN) vs port-and-verify (port → comprehensive tests → mutation-prove + cross-validate). The mutation-prove technique replaces the literal RED-first step when porting a known-good algorithm. Honesty rule: 'tests have caught a real regression' is the principle, not 'the test was committed before the impl.'

title: cas-core polynomial GCD: modular / sparse modular as v0.2
description: ADR-0013 landed Brown-Collins subresultant PRS as the v0.1 polynomial GCD. The follow-up: modular GCD (Brown's algorithm for univariate over Z; Brown-Yun-EZ-style for multivariate) for performance on dense or sparse inputs. Subresultant has polynomial coefficient bounds but no asymptotic edge over modular methods, and modular methods are dramatically faster on adversarial inputs (high-degree dense polynomials, large coefficient bit-widths). Implementation requires: prime selection / bound estimation, bad-prime detection (degree drop on reduction), CRT reconstruction, leading-coefficient lifting for multivariate. Defer until a workload demands it.
acceptance_criteria: packages/cas-core/src/poly-gcd-modular.ts (or similar) implements at least univariate Brown's; benchmark shows 10× or better on stress inputs (large coefficients, degree-50 univariate); both algorithms agree on correctness; existing subresultant kept as fallback for cases the modular path rejects.

title: runner.ts invariantToValue: use bool() helper
description:
packages/contract/src/runner.ts:108-110 builds { kind: '\''boolean'\'', value: inv.machine_checkable } as a raw kind-literal. CLAUDE.md says prefer the helpers from @workbench/protocol (bool, str, int, …).

scripts/check.ts:67-75 has a convention check that explicitly allowlists runner.ts to skip this drift. Don'\''t lean on the allowlist; lean on the helper. Replace the literal with bool(inv.machine_checkable). Once runner.ts is clean, also consider tightening the allowlist.
acceptance_criteria: runner.ts has no raw {kind:'\''...'\''} literals outside what is genuinely protocol-internal; allowlist in check.ts narrowed accordingly
close_reason: Fixed incidentally during the Schema landing (worklog 008). runner.ts now uses hashCanonicalBytes(outBytes) and provenanceToValue(rec); invariantToValue uses bool(); expr-parse self-test compares via canonicalize.

title: check.ts: remove dead _cmd parameter from spawnCmd alias
description:
scripts/check.ts:30: const spawnCmd = (_cmd: string, args: string[], stdin?: string) => spawnBun(args, stdin);

The _cmd parameter is unused — every call site passes '\''bun'\'' but only spawnBun runs. Either delete the alias entirely (callers use spawnBun directly) or genuinely route non-bun commands through it. The current shape is misleading.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/check.ts has no dead parameter; either spawnBun is called directly or spawnCmd handles non-bun cases meaningfully

title: Document gcd cost in rational validation
description:
packages/protocol/src/validate.ts:78-82 runs gcd(num, den) to verify '\''rational not in lowest terms'\''. Every parsed rational pays an O(log min(n, d)) cost. Acceptable — validation correctness is worth it — but unstated.

Add a one-line comment noting the deliberate cost and what alternative was rejected (eg. trusting upstream and skipping the check).
acceptance_criteria: validate.ts has a comment near the rational gcd block stating the cost and the deliberate choice

title: Comment NTT --test hook independent oracle rationale
description:
tools/ntt/tool.ts:191-245 reimplements pow, modInvSimple, rngBigint inline rather than importing from @workbench/mod-core. This is defensible — an independent oracle should be independent code, otherwise you'\''re testing that mod-core agrees with itself — but the rationale is not stated in the file.

Add a one-paragraph comment at the top of the test block explaining the deliberate independence.
acceptance_criteria: test hook in tools/ntt/tool.ts has a header comment explaining why pow/modInvSimple are inline rather than imported

value: Composition layer's single-implementation discipline: subprocess (runTool) and in-process (Workbench.run) MUST share executeToolDef so they produce byte-identical provenance for the same (tool, version, input, explicit-flags). 350+ goldens are the canary — if the in-process path ever diverges from subprocess output, it's a bug, not a degree of freedom. ADR-0012, packages/contract/src/execute.ts.

Composition layer DAG (c24 → ... → e0h, 9 issues) closed across 4 shards (032-035) on 2026-05-03. The TS-expert call site is @workbench/compose: loadWorkbench() returns the registry; typed(workbench) returns a TypedWorkbench extending Workbench with one method per tool plus the four non-tool surfaces (run, pipe, lookup, runMemoized). Demo-scope migration showed 7.4× full-suite speedup, ~20× on multi-step chains. Per-tool runtime contract (schema validate, fn, schema validate, canonicalise, write value+provenance+by-input index) lives in executeToolDef — runner.ts and Workbench.run share it; 350+ goldens are the byte-identicality canary.

Multi-device beads sync is set up via JSONL-over-git. Canonical fresh-clone command: `sh scripts/setup-device.sh` (sets core.hooksPath=.githooks, runs bd bootstrap --yes). NOT bd init or bd init --force — those rebuild the DB and discard issues. The tracked .githooks/pre-commit auto-runs bd export and stages .beads/issues.jsonl into every commit; .githooks/post-merge auto-runs bd import after every pull. The original blocker was a blanket .beads/ line in .git/info/exclude (set by bd init --stealth) — lifted in commit ef7dc19. Per-machine state (embeddeddolt/, backup/, interactions.jsonl, push-state.json, locks) stays gitignored via .beads/.gitignore. See worklog 027 for the full story including frictions.

THE TWO PRINCIPLES (universal decision rule for scientist-workbench, stated by the user 2026-05-04 as the highest-priority framework, supersedes any other framing):

1. What would a TypeScript expert expect/want?
2. It must be irresistible to agents (who are TS experts).

These are the same principle viewed from two sides: the agent IS the TS expert, so what (1) says is what (2) requires.

WHY: cited twice in the same session — first directing cas-diff's design, then again as a closing reminder after the tier-1 vocabulary extension shipped. It supersedes any other framework: "decomposition discipline," "honest scope," "agent-honest output" are *consequences* of the two principles, not separate axioms.

HOW TO APPLY:
- When in doubt, take a position. Don't escalate questions where the principles produce a clear answer.
- Apply them in commit messages and worklog "why" sections.
- Operational test: "a TS expert would type this without thinking" should be defensible. If it needs a paragraph of justification, the design is probably wrong.

CONCRETE EXAMPLES from this session:
- cas-diff input shape `{f, var}` (mirrors integrate-1d, predictable)
- cas-diff vocabulary matches integrate-1d/optimize, not cas-simplify (compose without scope translation)
- Tier-1 head naming: `asin`/`acos`/`atan` (matches Math.* — what TS reaches for reflexively)
- Smart constructors only in cas-diff, no internal cas-simplify call (one tool, one operation)

WRONG FRAMES TO AVOID:
- "What does Mathematica/SymPy do?" — irrelevant unless coincides with TS-expert want
- "What's the most general API?" — irrelevant if not what agent reaches for
- "What's the smallest surface?" — irrelevant if it forces caller assembly

SUBAGENTS ARE NOT THE DEFAULT. When a task is mechanical and well-specified by the principles, just do the work. Wrapping mechanical edits in a subagent prompt is a way of delegating the application of the principles, which the user has rejected (observed 2026-05-04: rejected subagent dispatch for tier-1 vocab extension; right move was to apply principles and edit directly). Subagents are for genuinely parallel independent work and contested-design research (CLAUDE.md Rule 4), not coordination overhead for routine implementation.

NARROWER COMPANION AXIOM: feedback_ts_native_design.md (auto-memory) and ADR-0009 — sturm-specific "don't port Julia idioms to TS." That memory predates the explicit universal statement of the two principles; it's a consequence of them applied to the sturm DSL design.
